cay_curator.text: Welcome to the Cayman National Museum. We've got turtle shells, sea chests, tall tales and a hat that belonged to a man who was never a pirate.

The islands were uninhabited when Columbus found them, and the first settlers were a mix of deserters, shipwrecked sailors, and enslaved people. Their descendants have been fishing, turtling and building ships here for centuries.
Ask anyone about the Wreck of the Ten Sail. Ask three people and you'll get four versions.

cay_schoolkid.text: Miss said we have to write down five things. I've written four. The fifth is that there's a stuffed turtle that looks sad.
Did you know it's called Cayman because of crocodiles? There aren't any. There's only this iguana.
